How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: IndiGo Ventures invests in Sarvam to enhance Artificial Intelligence in aviation
Article Text:
File photo: IndiGo

NEW DELHI: IndiGo Ventures, IndiGo’s corporate VC arm, will invest an undisclosed amount in Sarvam, India’s full-stack sovereign AI company, as part of Sarvam’s Series B round of funding. Announced Friday, the investment builds on the existing relationship between IndiGo and Sarvam who have been working together in multiple areas like enhancing customer experience and streamlining complex operational workflows across the airline through AI technologies.Neetan Chopra, IndiGo’s chief digital and information officer, said: “Artificial Intelligence is fast becoming a foundational capability for the aviation industry, reshaping customer experience, workforce productivity and operational decision-making.Our partnership with Sarvam gives IndiGo access to cutting-edge AI capabilities, built in India, and tailored to the needs of the market. By combining these technologies with our operational expertise and scale, we can accelerate innovation while maximising value for our customers, employees, and other stakeholders.”Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar said: “Aviation is a powerful setting for enterprise AI because it combines millions of customer interactions with complex, time-sensitive operations.IndiGo brings the domain depth and scale needed to identify where AI can create real value. Together, we can develop systems that are useful in production and build a stronger template for enterprise AI in India.”In a joint statement, the two companies said: “Aviation brings together high volumes of customer interactions, time-sensitive operations and a large, distributed workforce. The collaboration combines IndiGo’s core aviation expertise, operational scale and real-world use cases with Sarvam’s capabilities across AI models, voice and agentic systems to create a technology enabled, modern and future-ready airline infrastructure. IndiGo and Sarvam will continue to develop and evaluate applications across customer experience, employee productivity and airline operations, with the ability to expand successful use cases across IndiGo’s network.”IndiGo Ventures had three years ago received SEBI approval to establish an alternative investment fund (AIF) with a corpus of Rs 600 crore which is “committed to fostering innovation.”
Article Summary: IndiGo Ventures, IndiGo’s corporate VC arm, will invest an undisclosed amount in Sarvam. The investment builds on the existing relationship between the two companies. The two companies will continue to develop and evaluate applications across customer experience, employee productivity and airline operations.

Article Title: How a Chinese company is using Blue Light to fight mosquitoes, claims 30 kills per second: Scans the area, locks on in 3 milliseconds and...
Article Text:
Blue laser fires, mosquito drops: Photon Matrix claims 30 kills a second

How the Photon Matrix laser mosquito killer finds a 2mm target in the dark

The blue laser mosquito zapper's safety case has no independent testing behind it

The mosquito laser is a 20-year-old idea that finally shipped

Mosquitoes kill roughly 700,000 people a year, which makes them the deadliest animal on the planet by a wide margin. Our defences have not changed much in a century: nets, coils, sprays, and a rolled-up newspaper. A startup in Changzhou, in eastern China, thinks the next step is a laser turret that sits on your patio and shoots the insects out of the air.Photon Matrix has opened preorders for its blue laser mosquito air defense system at $1,088, roughly Rs 95,000, after starting mass production in August. The company says the device locks onto a mosquito in three milliseconds and can take down up to 30 of them a second, in complete darkness, without chemicals and without noise. Those are the company's own numbers, and nobody outside the company has verified them yet.The unit scans a flat fan of light across the space in front of it and continuously measures how far away the background is. When something small crosses that plane, the distance reading changes. The system then checks the size, and if it matches a mosquito, between 2mm and 20mm moving slower than a metre per second, an internal galvo mirror points the laser down the same optical path the LiDAR just used and burns the wings.Coverage is a six-metre radius across a 90-degree arc, and a rotating base spins the device for something closer to full coverage. A companion app logs kills, plots a mosquito heat map, sets on-off schedules and, for reasons known only to the marketing team, ranks you on a global leaderboard.The obvious question about a laser strong enough to disable an insect is what happens when it misses. Photon Matrix's answer is a background check: the laser fires only when it detects a solid surface within range, and shuts off when it cannot find one. The company says the system has cleared certifications covering people, pets and birds, and that it ignores butterflies and other larger insects. It has also promised to publish more testing and safety data. Until an independent reviewer gets a unit on a table, buyers are taking that on trust, and the comment sections under every video of this thing are full of people asking about eyes.There are two versions. The outdoor blue laser model at $1,088 flashes visibly each time it fires. The indoor infrared model, at $988 or about Rs 87,000, uses a 976nm invisible beam pitched at bedrooms and hotel rooms. Both come with a rotating base, a 12-month warranty and a 20,000mAh power bank good for around four hours off mains. Delivery is quoted at roughly 120 days.The project raised $2.7 million on Indiegogo against a $20,000 target, with over 4,000 backers paying about $630 each, then slipped repeatedly on sensor calibration and safety approvals. The concept itself dates to 2006, when an astrophysicist who worked on Reagan-era missile defence pitched it at a brainstorming session. A prototype turret with a 50-metre range was demonstrated in 2010 and never found a buyer.So the century-old arsenal gets a new entry, and it works out to about a thousand dollars for the privilege of watching mosquitoes fall.
Article Summary: Photon Matrix claims its laser can take down 30 mosquitoes a second. It uses a LiDAR to measure distance and size of the target. The laser fires only when it detects a solid surface within range, and shuts off when it cannot find one.

Article Title: Operation Bluebird startup launches Twitter.now, says it is not linked to Elon Musk's X
Article Text:
Operation Bluebird launches Twitter.now (AI-edited image)

A startup sees an opportunity after Twitter became X

A judge's comments gave the startup confidence to launch

Here’s what Operation Bluebird co-founder wrote on LinkedIn

The name Twitter has returned to the internet. A Virginia-based startup called Operation Bluebird has launched a new social media platform, Twitter.now, claiming that the Twitter name and some of its well-known intellectual property were abandoned after Elon Musk renamed Twitter to X. The launch comes despite an ongoing legal fight with X Corporation, which has challenged the startup's attempt to use the old Twitter identity. Operation Bluebird says its platform is not connected to X and is building a different kind of online public square, with automated fact-checking and more control for users over what they see.When Elon Musk acquired Twitter in 2022, he eventually renamed the platform X and replaced the familiar blue bird branding. Operation Bluebird believes that decision created an opportunity to reclaim the Twitter name.The startup's co-founder Stephen Coates, who previously served as general counsel at Twitter before Musk's takeover, said the company had waited for months before launching but did not want to delay further.Operation Bluebird's legal argument is that X Corporation abandoned its rights to trademarks linked to Twitter, including the word "Twitter," "tweet" and the bird logo. X Corporation, however, sued Operation Bluebird last year and sought to stop the new platform from launching.The legal dispute is still ongoing, and a final decision has not been issued.Legal dispute between Elon Musk’s X and Operation Bluebird continues.During an April 2026 hearing, US District Court Judge Colm Connolly gave a tentative ruling suggesting that X appeared to have given up its intellectual property claims over the word "tweet" and the Twitter bird logo. The judge also raised the possibility that rights to the word "Twitter" may have been abandoned.However, the judge has not yet issued a written order.The move could now intensify the legal battle. Trademark attorney Josh Gerben told Ars Technica that Operation Bluebird may have a workable legal argument, but said the case was far from straightforward and that X could respond strongly now that the platform has launched.In a LinkedIn post, Coates wrote:"Today, Operation Bluebird launched Twitter.now.When X Corp. retired the Twitter brand, we saw an opportunity to build something new: a public square organized around trust, transparency, and user choice.Twitter.now is not an attempt to recreate the old platform. We are building a different service, with trust signals that provide context for what users see and tools that allow people—not an opaque algorithm—to decide how much credibility and noise reach their feeds. Our governing principle is simple: freedom of speech, not freedom of reach.Twitter is a reclaimed brand. We are not X and are not affiliated with X Corp.Early access is now open. Founding members can help us build and test the platform, get first shot at the handle of their choice, and claim their place in its history—including Founder number #00001.The public square is open again, and definitely not affiliated with X in any way. Whatsoever.Get over your X. The bird is back."
Article Summary: Virginia-based startup Operation Bluebird has launched a new social media platform, Twitter.now. The launch comes despite an ongoing legal fight with X Corporation, which has challenged the startup's attempt to use the old Twitter identity. The legal dispute is still ongoing, and a final decision has not been issued.

Article Title: Apple 'Surprise and Shine' event on September 9: Foldable iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 Pro and everything else to expect
Article Text:
The foldable iPhone is the biggest launch expected on the day

The iPhone 18 Pro upgrade sounds modest, the price rise may not be

Watches, AirPods and new home devices make up the rest of the list

Siri AI is the software behind most of these new devices

Apple has confirmed September 9 for its annual iPhone launch, and the invite sent out on Wednesday uses the tagline "Surprise and shine." The keynote starts at 10am Pacific, which is 10.30pm IST, and will stream from the Steve Jobs Theater at Apple Park via Apple's site, YouTube and the Apple TV app.Two things separate this from the usual September routine. It is the first Apple event with John Ternus running the company, since Tim Cook hands over the CEO title on September 1 and becomes executive chairman. The rumoured product list is also unusually long. Apple pushed the new Mac mini and Mac Studio out in late August, a slot it has used only once in the past decade, and several reports read that as an attempt to free up space on stage.The device drawing the most attention is Apple's first foldable, which most reports expect to be called iPhone Ultra. Leaks point to a 7.8-inch inner display that opens like a book and a roughly 5.3-inch cover screen, with the A20 Pro chip and 12GB of memory.Rumours suggest two 48MP rear cameras and no telephoto lens, which would be an odd omission at this price. There are also claims that authentication falls back to Touch ID rather than Face ID.Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who says he has spoken to people who have used the phone, reports that the hinge and the way it fits in a pocket both impressed them, and that it works well as a camera viewfinder. He expects pricing to start above $2,000, roughly Rs 1.8 lakh before Indian duties, so the local figure would likely be higher.The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are widely tipped as a spec-bump year. Reports point to a 2nm A20 Pro with packaging changes meant to help thermals, Apple's own C2 modem, a slightly larger camera bump and a dark cherry finish. A variable-aperture rear camera is rumoured to be a Pro Max exclusive, and under-display Face ID has been floated without much backing.Pricing is the bigger question. With memory costs climbing, Samsung and Google have each raised phone prices by about $100, and Gurman expects Apple to follow, which would put the iPhone 18 Pro near $1,199. Other estimates run steeper.The standard iPhone 18, the iPhone 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air are not expected in September, with reports pointing to 2027.Apple Watch Series 12 is expected to be a light update, with talk of a health sensor tied to a fluoroelastomer band, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 may get a redesign. AirPods 5 look likely, in ANC and non-ANC versions. The camera-equipped AirPods that leaked in a macOS Tahoe release candidate are still reported as a 2027 product.The home devices are the bigger unknown. Reports mention a refreshed Apple TV 4K, a new HomePod mini and a home hub with a seven-inch screen. Gurman reports Apple is reworking the accessory sections in its retail stores, which he takes as a sign of more than routine updates. An OLED iPad mini remains a wildcard.Most of the home hardware has reportedly been waiting on the Siri overhaul Apple previewed at WWDC in June. That keynote was structured differently from the usual run through each operating system in turn, with Apple instead laying out a cross-platform pitch built around Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.The version demoed uses large language model technology to let the assistant act inside apps such as Messages and Calendar rather than only answering questions. It is the feature Apple has been promising and delaying since 2024.Siri AI is expected alongside iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Tahoe, watchOS 27 and tvOS 27, reportedly in the back half of September and initially as a waitlisted beta. That timing matters for the hardware. A refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini would need newer chips to support it, which is one explanation for why those updates have taken so long, and a home hub with a screen makes little sense without an assistant that can act on requests.
Article Summary: Apple will launch the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max on September 9. The foldable phone is expected to start at around $2,000. Apple Watch Series 12 and AirPods are expected to be light updates. Siri AI is expected alongside iOS 27, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27 and tvOS 27.

Article Title: Apple may launch AI-powered smart glasses in 202: Here’s what to expect
Article Text:
Apple smart glasses may use cameras to understand the real world

Apple smart glasses may use cameras to understand the real world

No display, but built-in speakers for music and calls

Health features may have to wait

Apple could make its entry into the smart glasses market as early as next year, with a product focused on artificial intelligence rather than augmented reality. According to reports, the company's first smart glasses are expected to combine cameras, Siri and built-in speakers to help users interact with the world around them, according to reports. Unlike AR glasses, they are not expected to have a display. Instead, users may be able to ask Siri questions about what they are seeing, translate signs and get information about their surroundings. Apple is also reportedly testing different designs as it prepares for a new category of AI-powered wearable devices.The reported glasses could use cameras and Apple's Visual Intelligence technology to help Siri understand what is around the wearer. This could allow users to ask questions about objects and places and receive relevant information.The glasses may also be able to translate text and signage. Another feature reportedly being considered would allow users to ask Siri to save an image of something and remind them about it later. However, the first-generation device may not work like a regular camera. Apple could reportedly limit the ability to take photos and videos, as privacy concerns around camera-equipped smart glasses continue to grow.Apple's first smart glasses are expected to be AI glasses rather than AR glasses. This means the device is not expected to place digital images or information directly in front of the user's eyes.Instead, the glasses could rely on voice commands, cameras and built-in speakers. The speakers could be used for music and other audio, potentially allowing the device to double as a pair of open-ear headphones.Apple is said to be developing the glasses in-house and is reportedly testing several designs. These include larger and slimmer rectangular frames, as well as oval and circular options. The frames could be made from acetate, a material considered more durable and premium than regular plastic. Reported colour options include black, ocean blue and light brown.Apple is reportedly also exploring health features for future versions of the smart glasses. These could include heart-rate monitoring and software tools designed to support fitness and wellness.But such features are not expected in the first version. For the initial model, Apple's focus appears to be on putting AI and Siri into a wearable device that could help users access information without having to constantly look at their phones.
Article Summary: Apple's first smart glasses are expected to be AI glasses rather than AR glasses. Apple is said to be developing the glasses in-house and is reportedly testing several designs.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang missing from Time's 100 most influential people in AI list for 2026
Article Text:
Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia.

Jensen Huang missing from Time 100 AI 2026 list

Elon Musk, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei appear in the list

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company has become one of the biggest suppliers of chips powering the artificial intelligence boom, has been left off Time magazine's 2026 list of the 100 most influential people in AI. The omission has drawn attention because Jensen Huang featured on the list in each of its first three editions, starting in 2023. The 2026 list includes several prominent figures from technology, business and entertainment, including Elon Musk , OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.Time says its annual list recognises people who are shaping the key developments in artificial intelligence and influencing the technology's growth.Jensen Huang's absence stands out given Nvidia's central role in the AI industry. The company's graphics processing units, or GPUs, are widely used to train and run advanced AI systems, making Nvidia a major player in the rapid growth of the sector.Notably, Jensen Huang was included in Time's AI 100 lists in 2023, 2024 and 2025. However, he does not appear on the 2026 list.Time described the purpose of its list as identifying people who “best represent the year’s key storylines” and who are having the most influence on developments in AI.Several of the biggest names in AI are featured on this year's list. These include SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. The list also includes executives and leaders associated with companies including IBM, Google DeepMind, ByteDance, Broadcom, Databricks, Amazon and Oracle.Beyond technology leaders, the 2026 list also features names from entertainment and politics, including Ben Affleck, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Paris Hilton and US Senator Bernie Sanders.Time 100 AI list highlights changing influence in AITime's list is not a ranking of companies or a direct measure of business success. Instead, the publication selects people it believes have had significant influence on the major AI developments of the year. As a result, the list changes from year to year and can include researchers, business leaders, policymakers and public figures alongside technology executives.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang featured on the list in each of its first three editions, starting in 2023. The 2026 list includes several prominent figures from technology, business and entertainment. Elon Musk, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei appear in the list. The omission stands out given Nvidia's central role in the AI industry.

Article Title: Google Messages gets customisation setting: How to use it
Article Text:
Key requirements before getting started

How to change Google Messages chat theme step by step

Launch the Google Messages app on your phone.

Open the specific conversation you want to restyle.

Tap the three-dot menu located in the top-right corner of the display.

Select Chat theme from the dropdown menu to open the customization screen.

Google is officially rolling out dedicated chat theme customisation for its Google Messages texting platform, allowing users to personalise the look and feel of individual conversations with distinct colour palettes and custom background wallpapers. While personalising themes has long been standard across rival messaging clients, the option is now reaching users across both stable and beta versions of Google Messages. In this article, we will explain how to step-by-step change your Messages background.To access the new theming engine, users need to meet two essential requirements on their Android devices. First, check the Google Play Store by tapping your profile icon, selecting Manage apps & device, reviewing Updates available, and updating Google Messages to its newest release.Second is enable RCS Messaging as chat themes operate exclusively over RCS. To verify that the feature is enabled, open up Google Messages, tap the profile icon in the top-right corner, go to Messages settings, tap RCS chats and make sure the Turn on RCS chats toggle is switched on.To turn on a custom theme, just tap a few times inside any conversation thread:The theme settings panel gives users two main styling tools for customizing the visual interface: Chat colors Custom & curated wallpapers:Every theme and background change is completely local and private. The color accents you choose or custom wallpaper choices will not be seen on the screens of recipients in your one-on-one threads or group chats.
Article Summary: Google is officially rolling out dedicated chat theme customisation for its Google Messages texting platform. Users can personalise the look and feel of individual conversations with distinct colour palettes and custom background wallpapers. The option is now reaching users across both stable and beta versions of Google Messages.

Article Title: Elon Musk breaks silence on OpenAI cutting 3-year-old deal with Cursor over him; says: Sam Altman is …
Article Text:
Elon Musk breaks silence on OpenAI cutting 3-year-old deal with Cursor

‘Cursor was one of the very first users of OpenAI’

Here’s what OpenAI said on cutting off deal with Cursor

Elon Musk has responded after OpenAI said it is ending its partnership with Cursor, a coding tool recently acquired by Musk's SpaceX. The move ends a partnership that had been in place for around three years and adds a new chapter to the long-running dispute between Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. In an X (formerly Twitter) post, Musk appeared unfazed by the decision, saying he “couldn’t care less” and launching a fresh attack on Altman and OpenAI President Greg Brockman, calling them untrustworthy. “I couldn’t care less. Scam Altman and Greg Stockman are utterly untrustworthy assholes who stole an open source nonprofit,” Musk wrote in the post.Cursor was founded in 2022. It was recently acquired by Elon Musk’s space company SpaceX. Musk had sued OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman for "stealing a charity" by betraying the company's ​original nonprofit mission.“To work with a large partner like SpaceX, we typically rely on custom contracts to ensure compliance with our terms of service and that the integration provides for safety at scale. After Musk acquired Twitter, now part of SpaceX, the company broke⁠(opens in a new window) the terms of our contract (alongside many others).Under oath earlier this year, Musk admitted⁠(opens in a new window) that xAI, now also part of SpaceX, had violated OpenAI’s terms of service (terms which are similar to xAI’s own),” OpenAI said in an announcement.Reacting to the OpenAI announcement, Michael Truell, a co-founder of Cursor and now an executive at SpaceX shared an X post where he reiterated that Cursor was one of the very first users of OpenAI and that the space company is “speaking with the OpenAI team to resolve this”.“We’re sorry to see that OpenAI put out a note saying they plan to block Cursor users from accessing OpenAI models in three months,” Truell wrote in the post adding “OpenAI models serve about 5% of Cursor user traffic, and we’re speaking with the OpenAI team to resolve this”.“Cursor was one of the very first users of OpenAI, we’ve worked closely with their team for years, and we’ve trusted their platform to be neutral infrastructure for our business.”"Today, we notified SpaceX that we intend to wind down our contract providing OpenAI models to Cursor, with a proposed shutoff date of November 12, 2026. To maximize the time that developers can retain access to our models through Cursor, we are giving the maximum notice provided by our contract. This decision was incredibly tough, as we care deeply about our models being broadly available for developers. We are making this choice because we cannot be confident that SpaceX will use our technology within our terms of service, based on our experience with Elon Musk's companies violating contracts.To work with a large partner like SpaceX, we typically rely on custom contracts to ensure compliance with our terms of service and that the integration provides for safety at scale. After Musk acquired Twitter, now part of SpaceX, the company broke⁠(opens in a new window) the terms of our contract (alongside many others). Under oath earlier this year, Musk admitted⁠(opens in a new window) that xAI, now also part of SpaceX, had violated OpenAI’s terms of service (terms which are similar to xAI’s own).Our custom agreement with Cursor gives us a limited time window to cancel it after a change of control. As AI capabilities advance, we also have a new level of accountability to ensure our upcoming model, Astra, is being used in accordance with our terms. Given all of this, we’ve decided to hold the contract cancellation to the latest date we can while not providing future models to Cursor.We’ve worked with Cursor for nearly four years and have enormous respect for their team, their product, and what they’ve built for the developer community. We know that the people most affected by this decision are the developers who rely on OpenAI models in Cursor. We care about their experience in this transition and we’re ready to go above and beyond to support them."

In an X (formerly Twitter) post, Musk appeared unfazed by the decision, saying he “couldn’t care less” and launching a fresh attack on Altman and Open AI President Greg Brockman.

Article Title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman warns of a ‘critically important moment’ for cyber defense as AI …
Article Text:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman

Sam Altman: There is not much time to act

Why Sam Altman is calling for a collective response

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has issued an urgent warning about the growing challenges artificial intelligence could bring to cybersecurity, saying there is “not much time to act” and calling for a collective response from across the technology industry. In a recent post on X, formerly Twitter, Sam Altman described the current period as a “critically important moment for cyber defense with AI.” His message comes as AI tools become increasingly powerful, raising concerns about how the same technology that can help security teams defend computer systems could also be used by malicious actors.In the post, Altman urged people working in cybersecurity to take the moment seriously, saying the response cannot be limited to one company.“This is a critically important moment for cyber defense with AI; there is not much time to act,” Sam Altman wrote in the post. He said OpenAI would welcome people who want to work with the company, but also stressed that its competitors and partners have a role to play.“We are happy if you want to work with us or any of our competitors or partners, but please take this moment seriously,” he wrote.The message suggests that Altman sees AI-driven cybersecurity as an industry-wide challenge rather than a competition that can be addressed by a single company.AI is increasingly being used to automate tasks, analyse large amounts of data and identify patterns quickly. These abilities can help cyber defenders find threats faster. But they can also create new risks if advanced AI capabilities are misused.Sam Altman did not provide specific details about the threats that prompted his warning in the post. However, he made clear that he believes a coordinated response is needed.“Only an urgent and intense collective response will work,” Altman wrote.
Article Summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has issued an urgent warning about the growing challenges artificial intelligence could bring to cybersecurity. He said there is “not much time to act” and called for a collective response from across the technology industry. Altman did not provide specific details about the threats that prompted his warning.

Article Title: An AI-powered Iron Dome is promising to protect California residents from what it calls the world’s deadliest creatures, mosquitoes
Article Text:
Image credit: X

West Nile cases climb in California

How the device tracks and kills mosquitoes

Indoor and outdoor versions, at a price

As West Nile Virus creeps into California, a new AI-powered mosquito killer could be just what Californians need to protect them from the world's deadliest creature.The Photon Matrix is a high-tech zapper that combines futuristic light detection and ranging technology (LiDAR), radar, with AI directing a precision laser to detect mosquitoes and zap them dead with a blue laser. It's been dubbed "an Iron Dome for mosquitoes" by one robotics commentator on X.According to the Chinese start-up, the device is designed to target multiple kinds of mosquitoes, but avoids other flying insects like butterflies.Warmer temperatures have increased the mosquito population and lengthened mosquito season in recent years. Earlier this month, the second Californian this year died from West Nile Virus, a deadly mosquito-borne disease.Earlier this month, the California Department of Public Health has reported 30 human cases of the disease, a five-year high.The virus produces no symptoms in 80% of cases, but in severe ones, those infected may experience fever, severe headache, stiff neck, rash, joint pain, confusion, and altered consciousness.Photon Matrix's device can reportedly detect and kill insects as small as 2mm flying at speeds of up to 3.3 feet per second."Our intelligent mosquito air defense system is powered by LiDAR detection and targeting technology," the company said on its website. "By combining AI vision, real-time tracking and precision laser elimination, it creates a smarter and chemical-free solution for physical mosquito control."The device's LiDAR scanner has a target range of 20 feet, and its zaps are "quieter than a whisper," according to the company. Videos of the outdoor version show the device putting on a light show when activated, zapping mosquitoes with its bright blue lasers.The company is also selling an indoor version of the device, which uses infrared detection and a laser invisible to the human eye.The outdoor version is available for $1,088, while the indoor version retails for $988.
Article Summary: The Photon Matrix is a high-tech zapper that tracks and kills mosquitoes. It combines light detection and ranging technology (LiDAR), radar, with AI directing a precision laser to detect mosquitoes and zap them dead with a blue laser. It's been dubbed "an Iron Dome for mosquitoes" by one robotics commentator.
